Subject: Redwood rehearsal — clarifications on RTO/RPO and region ordering

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Tuesday. As we prepare our vendor DR rehearsal schedule with the SRE and compliance teams, we need a few clarifications from Redwood so we can finalize the Mutual Action Plan:

- Can you confirm typical RTO and RPO targets for single-region loss (control plane unaffected) for our production workload (avg. seq len 512, steady-state QPS ~650)?
- During a controlled failover test, what exact client-visible impacts should our app teams expect (latency bump, brief 503s, partial feature degradation)?
- If we prioritize traffic to us-east-1 over us-west-2 during a regional outage, can you describe the steps Redwood takes to drain KV caches and warm new instances to avoid cold-start token penalties?

We’re targeting the week of 3/27 for a non-disruptive dry-run and 4/10 for a formal rehearsal with our compliance observers. Before we lock dates, please send any runbook or playbook you recommend, and confirm whether you can provide an on-call engineer for the rehearsal window.

Thanks — we want to ensure the rehearsal meets our audit requirements without putting production at undue risk.

Aisha
Aisha Khan
Cloud Ops Lead — PrimeHealth Systems

Subject: Re: Redwood rehearsal — clarifications on RTO/RPO and region ordering

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front, full details below and an attached playbook: Redwood_DR_Rehearsal_Playbook_v1.pdf.

- Baseline targets: RTO (regional switchover): <= 3 minutes for control-plane-aware clients; visible recovery (steady-state tokens flowing): ~5–8 minutes depending on prefix cache hit rates. RPO: best-effort for in-flight token state; durable artifacts (logs/metrics) replicated within <60s to secondary telemetry stores.
- Client-visible impacts: short latency increase (~20–60% for 3–8 minutes) during KV cache warm, occasional 429s as we rehydrate batching windows, and transient 503s for misrouted long-running requests.
- Cache warm strategy: we do a prioritized prefix rehydration using recent prefixes + predictive warmers tied to your route weights. We will not proactively evict customer-level KV unless explicitly requested.

Proposed next steps:
1) Vivek to propose the technical sequence for the rehearsal (drain, cutover, validation).
2) Karthik to confirm coverage for support credits and on-call for that window.
3) Mutual Action Plan (we’ll draft) and you to add any audit evidence fields.

We can commit a senior engineer to the 4/10 rehearsal; 3/27 dry-run coverage will be by our platform on-call. I’ll attach the playbook and a short checklist.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

Subject: Technical: rehearsal sequence and expected metrics

Hi all —

Detailing the technical sequence we recommend for the rehearsal. This is the order we will run in the dry-run and the formal test:

1) Readiness check (0m): validate control plane health, capacity tokens, and routing table.
2) Pre-warm (2–5m): spin warm instances in us-east-1; prefetch top-50 prefixes from recent traffic to prime KV caches.
3) Traffic shift (3–6m): reroute 90% of traffic to us-east-1 via our smart routing layer; keep 10% on the origin for canary validation.
4) Warm stabilization (6–12m): monitor 95th/99th latency, error rates, and token emission rate. Expect latency uplift up to ~0.6x at p95 for 6–8 minutes if cache hit-rate is low.
4a) If errors > threshold (p99 errors > 2%), abort and rollback to origin within target <2m.
5) Final validation (12–18m): run synthetic queries and validate checksum of embeddings/outputs for determinism checks where applicable.

Notes on RPO semantics: our inference runtime does not provide transactional guarantees for in-flight token sequences; clients should use idempotency keys for critical state. Durable logs, audit trails, and usage metrics are asynchronously replicated with TTL <60s to secondary stores; for regulatory attestations we can provide export of those logs post-test.

Operational hooks we’ll provide during the rehearsal:
- live tracing links and token-level cost breakdowns by route
- per-model KV hit-rate dashboard
- one-click rollback button in the console (executes routing swap and instance drain)

I’ll also share a short snippet the on-call can run to force a graceful drain:

> # drain command (runtime admin)
> redwood runtime drain --pool prod-us-west-2 --target us-east-1 --grace 120

We can run the pre-warm and traffic-shift steps in the dry-run with no customer TTL expiry to avoid data loss.

-Vivek
Principal Architect — Redwood Inference
